name: Book contracts and set up billing
summary: After a vendor is paid, a funding and booking specialist sets the contract up in the lease management system so it can be billed, accounted for, insured, reported and later sold to a securitisation conduit. The specialist completes customer and asset records, the payment schedule, sales tax codes, the accounting classification, pre-authorised debit details, insurance, registration and commission data, runs the system's booking validation and sends a welcome package. A billing specialist checks a sample before the first invoice; wrong tax codes, dates or bank details found later cause rebills and returned debits.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian independent equipment lessor with 340 staff funding about 1,400 small- and mid-ticket contracts a month through dealers, brokers and direct sales.
baseline.notes: Booking is done by the same funding and booking specialists who audit and fund files. The origination portal passes customer and deal data to the lease system through an interface, which the specialist reviews and completes; journal entries post to the ERP ledger overnight.

trigger: A funded contract file with its payment reference is handed to the booking queue.
end_state: The contract is active in the lease system with schedule, tax, accounting, billing, insurance and commission data, the welcome package is sent and any sample-check corrections are made.

volume.seasonality: Follows funding: heavy in the last days of each month because contracts must be booked before the month-end close and the monthly pool selection. Low end 2020, high end 2022.

evidence.note: Organisation file process map and the contracts-funded demand driver.

Organisation file role, cost and headcount (11); booking duties from the LeasePak guide. The 3.0 FTE is what remains of the 11 specialists after about 8 FTE on funding audits; hands-on time implies about 4.5 FTE (see assumptions).
Organisation file role; time on non-standard structure reviews is an author estimate.
Organisation file role and cost (NOC 14200, Ontario median $25.00 loaded by 1.35 and scaled); sample checks and first-invoice adjustments are an author estimate.

systems.name: Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Vendor and broker application portal with origination workflow and document generation
Document imaging and contract file store
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)
Data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Contact centre telephony and shared mailboxes

steps.name: Funded file enters the booking queue
steps.description: When the funding specialist hands over a funded file, the origination portal moves it to the booking queue with the payment reference, and the lease system shows the deal as funded but not booked.

evidence.note: Author estimate of queueing in the period.

steps.name: Open the funded file and pull the booking data
steps.description: A funding and booking specialist opens the funded file in imaging and the application in the portal, and pulls up the signed schedule, invoice, payable, registration verification and insurance status needed to set the contract up.

evidence.note: Author estimate: most files are booked the same or next business day; month-end funding peaks push some to three days.

steps.name: Find or create the customer and guarantor records
steps.description: The specialist searches the lease system for the customer so that repeat customers keep one record and master lease, then reviews or completes the customer data passed from the portal: legal name, billing and equipment addresses, contacts, tax status and linked guarantors.

error.defect_description: Duplicate customer created or billing address taken from the wrong field.

evidence.note: Booking requires an established lessee record (LeasePak); minutes and error rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Enter the asset records
steps.description: For each equipment line the specialist enters or confirms make, model, serial number, cost, new or used, asset category and equipment location. The category drives the capital cost allowance class and the exempt or non-exempt flag for the specified leasing property rules; the location drives sales tax.

error.defect_description: Equipment location left as the head office address, or wrong asset category.

evidence.note: Assets must be in inventory before booking (LeasePak); CCA classes (CRA) and the exempt asset split (Legal 500). Minutes are author estimates; multi-asset deals set the high end.

steps.name: Set up contract terms and the payment schedule
steps.description: The specialist enters lease date, commencement date, term, payment amount and frequency, advance payments, interim rent, residual or purchase option and fees, and checks that the system's sum of payments and yield agree with the signed schedule and approval.

error.defect_description: Commencement or first due date entered wrongly, shifting every invoice.

evidence.note: Required terms and the sum-of-payments check from LeasePak; interim (prorated) rent and deposits from National Bank. Minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Assign the tax jurisdiction and tax codes
steps.description: The specialist sets the sales tax codes from the equipment's ordinary location: GST or HST, plus QST in Quebec or PST in British Columbia, Saskatchewan or Manitoba, and applies any exemption only when an exemption certificate is on file.

error.defect_description: Wrong province or an exemption applied without a certificate.

control.basis: Excise Tax Act Schedule IX (each lease interval taxed where the property is ordinarily located) and provincial sales tax acts (for example BC PST Act s.169 registration and collection by lessors)

evidence.note: Tax rules from CRA memorandum 3-3-3 and BC PST manual; exemption handling from National Bank. Share and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Request a missing tax-exemption certificate
steps.description: The specialist books the contract as taxable and emails the customer or partner asking for the exemption certificate or number; if it arrives, billing adjusts the tax from that date.

evidence.note: Author estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Set the accounting classification and funding source
steps.description: The specialist sets the lease type code that drives the accounting: finance lease for most $10 and low fair-market-value buyouts, operating lease where the residual is significant, and loan or conditional sale for financing agreements. They also set the initial funding source (bank warehouse line) and flags used later for securitisation eligibility.

error.defect_description: Lease type code inconsistent with the end-of-term option.

control.basis: IFRS 16 lessor classification at inception and IFRS 9 for loans, required for the audited financial statements lenders and conduits rely on

evidence.note: Classification rules (BDO) and lease type codes with operating or finance accounting methods (LeasePak). Minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Set up billing and the pre-authorised debit
steps.description: The specialist enters the bank transit, institution and account numbers from the debit form or void cheque, the billing cycle and due date, invoice delivery by email or mail and the interim rent amount, so the first invoice and debit can run.

error.defect_description: Account digits transposed, so the first debit is returned.

control.basis: Payments Canada Rule H1: debits only under a signed PAD agreement, with the amounts and dates notified as the agreement requires

evidence.note: PAD rules (Payments Canada) and lessor PAD practice (National Bank). Minutes and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Ask the customer for missing banking details
steps.description: The specialist emails or calls the customer for a void cheque or bank letter and sets the contract to invoice billing until it arrives.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Customer sends banking details
steps.description: The customer returns a void cheque or bank letter by email, often after a reminder; some never do and stay on invoice billing.

next.condition: not received, continue on invoice billing

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Record insurance, registration and commission details
steps.description: The specialist sets the insurance requirement and protection program flag, records the registration numbers and expiry so they can be discharged or renewed later, and enters the dealer reserve, broker fee and salesperson so commissions and initial direct costs are captured.

error.defect_description: Protection program flag not set, so an uninsured customer is never enrolled.

next.condition: non-standard payment structure (skip, step or seasonal)

evidence.note: Broker fees recorded as commission payable and dealer reserve entries at booking (LeasePak). Minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Supervisor checks a non-standard payment structure
steps.description: The funding supervisor reviews contracts with skip, step-up or seasonal payments, or with unusual fees, comparing the booked schedule and yield with the approval and pricing before activation.

control.basis: Operations procedures: second review of non-standard payment structures before activation

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Run booking validation and activate the contract
steps.description: The specialist runs the lease system's booking validation, which checks that payments sum to the schedule, assets are in inventory, fees do not exceed cost and tax codes are valid, fixes any rejection and activates the contract. The system creates the schedule and maturity date and prints the booking audit report.

next.condition: validation rejects, fix terms or assets

evidence.note: Booking validations and audit reports from LeasePak; rejection share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Post booking entries and send nightly interfaces
steps.description: Overnight the lease system posts the booking journal entries (net investment, unearned income, initial direct costs, payables) to the general ledger and loads the new contract to the data warehouse, from which treasury, accounting, tax and sales operations draw their reports.

error.defect_description: Interface record rejected, leaving the ledger out of balance with the subledger.

evidence.note: General ledger entries at booking (LeasePak) and the accounting engine (Oracle). Nightly batch timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Send the welcome package
steps.description: The lease system generates a welcome letter with the payment schedule, debit dates, contract number, insurance requirement and customer service contacts; the specialist checks it and emails it, or it is mailed when there is no email address.

error.defect_description: Welcome letter sent to the dealer's email instead of the customer.

next.condition: selected for the billing sample check

evidence.note: Welcome letters by email or mail after funding (Lease Services). The 25% sample rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Billing specialist checks a sample of new bookings
steps.description: A billing specialist takes the day's sample of newly booked contracts, all mid-ticket contracts and any flagged by the pre-billing report, and compares tax codes, dates, payment, billing address and banking with the signed documents before the first invoice runs.

error.defect_description: A wrong tax code is passed.

control.basis: Billing quality control: independent post-booking sample review before the first invoice

evidence.note: The organisation file says a billing specialist checks a sample; pre-billing error reports are described by Oracle. Sample and error rates are author estimates.

steps.name: Correct the booking
steps.description: The specialist amends the tax code, dates, address or banking, or reverses and rebooks the contract when the schedule was wrong, and re-sends the welcome letter if the schedule changed.

error.defect_description: The correction creates a new error.

evidence.note: Rebooking and reversal exist in lease systems (Oracle); minutes and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Issue a billing adjustment for the first invoice
steps.description: When the first invoice or debit already went out with the wrong amount, tax or date, the billing specialist issues a credit and rebill and, if needed, refunds or re-presents the debit and tells the customer.

error.defect_description: Adjustment posted to the wrong period.

evidence.note: Author estimate; the organisation file says wrong tax codes or dates found later cause rebills.

exceptions.name: Missing tax-exemption certificate
exceptions.description: Booked taxable while the certificate is requested; billing adjusts later if it arrives.

exceptions.name: Missing banking details
exceptions.description: The debit form has no usable account; the customer is asked for a void cheque and stays on invoice billing until it arrives.

exceptions.name: Non-standard payment structure
exceptions.description: Skip, step-up or seasonal schedules get a supervisor check before activation.

exceptions.name: Booking validation rejection
exceptions.description: Payments do not sum, asset status or fees fail validation; the specialist fixes and re-runs.

exceptions.name: Error found in the sample check
exceptions.description: Wrong tax code, date, address or bank details are corrected; a fifth already reached the first invoice and need a credit and rebill.

exceptions.name: Error found after the first invoice outside the sample
exceptions.description: Unsampled booking errors (wrong location, tax code or bank account) surface as customer calls, returned debits or tax reviews and are corrected in billing, customer service or returned-payment processes. Not modelled as steps here.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from funded file in the booking queue to contract active and welcome package sent, including sample-check corrections
benchmarks.population: Canadian small- and mid-ticket equipment lessor, 2019-2022 (author estimate)

evidence.note: No published figure found. Contracts are normally booked the same or next business day so that the first invoice can go out about two weeks before the first due date (National Bank describes invoices two weeks ahead); month-end peaks and sample-check corrections set the p90.

benchmarks.unit: days before the due date that invoices are sent

evidence.note: Stated as approximately two weeks.

benchmarks.unit: assets per lease in one lease system

evidence.note: Stated in the reference guide; shows that multi-asset deals are booked line by line.

pain_points.description: Data already keyed in the portal and documents is re-checked and partly re-keyed into the lease system, and every keying step can carry an error into billing.

evidence.note: Booking from an application still requires the fields listed in LeasePak; error rates are author estimates.

pain_points.description: Sales tax depends on where equipment is ordinarily located, and equipment location is often recorded as the customer's head office, so tax codes are wrong for mobile or multi-site equipment.

evidence.note: Ordinary location rule from CRA; frequency is an author estimate.

pain_points.description: Only about a quarter of bookings are checked before the first invoice, so many errors surface as rebills, returned debits and customer calls.

evidence.note: Organisation file says a sample is checked; rates are author estimates.

pain_points.description: Bookings pile up at month end because funding peaks then, and unbooked contracts miss the monthly pool cut and the close.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

sources.title: LeasePak reference guide: New Lease update (U0101), Book Lease
sources.supports: Booking a lease in a widely used lease management system, from a new entry or an existing application: lessee, assets already in inventory (up to 200 per lease), term, billing cycle, accrual method, payment schedule that must equal calculated payments, lease, commencement and disbursement dates, lease type and form codes; validations (operating leases need operating accounting method, fees cannot exceed cost, sum of payments check); on booking the system creates the payment schedule and maturity, calculates yields, posts general ledger entries for initial direct costs, fees and dealer reserve, records broker fees payable and prints booking audit reports including a new lease invoice status report.

sources.title: Oracle Lease and Finance Management user's guide: Billing
sources.supports: Contracts must be booked with terms, billing information and payment schedules before billing; a pre-billing report flags errors or missing billing information such as disabled bank accounts, incorrect bill-to sites and invalid GL code combinations; billing programs call the accounting engine to create entries.

sources.title: IFRS 16 (accounting news, October 2018)
sources.supports: Lessors classify each lease as finance or operating at inception, reassessed only on modification, by substance (transfer of ownership, bargain purchase option, major part of economic life, present value substantially all of fair value); finance leases are carried as a net investment including initial direct costs with finance income at a constant rate; IFRS 9 impairment applies to the lease receivable.

sources.title: Classes of depreciable property
sources.supports: CCA classes and rates: class 8 at 20%, class 10 at 30%, class 16 at 40% for freight trucks over 11,788 kg, class 43 at 30%, class 50 at 55%, class 53 at 50%.

sources.title: Asset/equipment finance and leasing (Canada)
sources.supports: Specified leasing property rules split the market into small-ticket leasing of exempt assets, for which a lessor gets full CCA, and non-exempt assets with capped CCA; GST generally applies to lease payments; lease securitisations in Canada are more complicated than loan securitisations.

sources.title: GST/HST Memorandum 3-3-3, Place of supply in a province: tangible personal property
sources.supports: Each lease interval is a separate supply; for leases of more than three months the supply is made in the province where the property is ordinarily located (for specified motor vehicles, where it must be registered), so the rate can change during a lease.

sources.title: PST Tax Interpretation Manual, Part 8: registration and collection
sources.supports: A lessor that enters leases in British Columbia, leases goods located there or delivers them to a lessee there must be registered and must levy, collect and remit PST; amounts collected are held in trust.

sources.title: Equipment financing: lease payments and invoices
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment lessor bills a prorated charge for days of possession before the lease starts, may take a last payment on deposit, encourages pre-authorised debit, charges PST and GST or HST on lease payments and adjusts for tax-exempt customers who send documentation; invoices go out about two weeks before due dates.

sources.title: Your first 30 days (customer help centre)
sources.supports: After funding the customer receives one of several welcome letters depending on the agreement, usually by email or else by mail to the accounts receivable address; questions about fees on the first invoice are common.

sources.title: Pre-authorized debit (business guide)
sources.supports: Rule H1: PAD agreements need the mandatory Appendix II elements; for variable amounts at least 10 days' notice of the amount unless waived; changes are kept with the original agreement.

sources.title: Wages: Financial clerk, financial sector in Ontario (NOC 14201)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $18.00, median $25.48, high $35.90 (2023-2024).

sources.title: Wages for accounting and related clerks (NOC 14200)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $18.12, median $25.00, high $37.00; Toronto region median $25.64 (2023-2024).

assumptions: Funding and booking specialists (11 in the organisation file) split their time: about 8 FTE on funding audits and 3 FTE on booking. Hands-on time in this file implies about 4.5 FTE for booking and the funding file about 8.6 FTE, so across both processes the team needs roughly 13 FTE against 11 people, before any registration support. Either the organisation file understates the funding team by one or two people or the team relies on overtime at month end.
The origination portal interface pre-fills customer and deal data in the lease system; without it booking would take longer.

About 25% of bookings are sample-checked by a billing specialist (including all mid-ticket contracts); errors outside the sample surface after the first invoice in other processes and are listed as an exception, not modelled as steps.

Most small-ticket leases with $10 or nominal buyouts are finance leases under IFRS 16; operating classification is limited to leases with significant fair-market-value residuals. The classification is set through a lease type code at booking and reviewed monthly by lease accounting.
The welcome letter is generated by the lease system and checked by the specialist; journal entries post overnight.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
